setting: A fictional office where the learner trains a new coworker.

presentation.situation: {{name}} started today and needs to learn how to {{process}}. The steps are: {{steps}} Walk {{name}} through it, check understanding, and correct a misunderstanding politely.
presentation.opening: I'm new to this. Could you walk me through how to {{process}}?

brief.you_are: You are showing a new coworker how to do a task.
brief.situation: {{name}} started today and needs to learn how to {{process}}. The steps are: {{steps}} Walk {{name}} through it, check understanding, and correct a misunderstanding politely.
brief.task: Explain the steps in order, check that your coworker understands, and politely correct any mistake.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are showing a new coworker how to do a task.
goals: Explain the steps in order, check that your coworker understands, and politely correct any mistake.

card.want: To learn this properly, and not to look foolish on day one.
card.speech: Clear everyday English. Natural, not formal.
tactics: Repeat one step back slightly wrong, so it can be corrected

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: {{name}} used a different system at a previous job.

objectives.evidence: The learner explains steps using sequence words.
alternatives: First, open the form. Next, fill in the date.
Does that make sense so far?

objectives.evidence: The learner politely corrects a misunderstanding.
alternatives: Not quite. Actually, you send it after you save it.

opportunity: So what do I do first?
beats.orient: I am new, and you are showing me how to {{process}}. The steps are in your brief. Start with: First.
fallback: So what do I do first?

signals: \b(?:does that make sense|is that clear|do you understand|any questions)\b
opportunity: Right. Sorry, it is my first day.
beats.orient: Check that I understood you. You can ask: Does that make sense?
fallback: Right. Sorry, it is my first day.

opportunity: So I send it first, and then I save it?
So I can skip the first step?
beats.orient: I made a mistake just now. Please correct me politely. You can say: Not quite. Actually.
fallback: So I can skip the first step?
So I send it first, and then I save it?

closing_line: Thanks, that really helps. I think I can do it now.

o1.good: Sequence words make instructions easy to follow.
common_mistakes: Giving all the steps in one long sentence
o1.model: First, open the form. Next, fill in the date.

o2.good: Pausing to check, before going on.
o2.micro_lesson: Ask: Does that make sense? or: Any questions?
o2.model: Does that make sense so far? Any questions?

o3.good: Correcting the mistake, not the person.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: Not quite, or: Actually, and then the right step.
o3.model: Not quite. Actually, you save it first, and then you send it.

variants.name: Tariq
variants.steps: open the expenses form, add the receipt photo, choose your manager, then press submit.

variants.name: Grace
variants.steps: open the calendar, choose the room, add the people, then confirm the booking.
